blindSummary:
A provincial-level assembly within this state/province certified and affirmed a 2023 municipal ordinance protecting the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex people (recorded in a provincial board resolution of 2024, session of 19 August 2024) - a provincial-level endorsement of a municipal LGBTQ+ protection ordinance in a conservative part of the country. This gives a visitor travelling the main corridor through this state/province a local complaint route absent in most other units of the country.

Against that, two constituent areas within this state/province are home to a codified customary-justice system of indigenous communities, with its own dispute-resolution authority over “crimes and tribal-related offences,” recognised by the country's courts. No trans-specific customary ruling or exclusion was documented, but the legal-pluralism structure means that in a rural dispute in those areas, the applicable institution may not be a national court.

Net direction: slightly above the country-wide average - modest because the protective ordinance is municipal and the plural-justice uncertainty is localised to those two areas. A neighbouring state/province offers a broader ordinance cluster (city-level implementing rules backed by a UN development programme, unanimous municipal votes) and has no countervailing alternative-justice structure.
